questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Mali?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Mali article.

questions.proof: Mali's capital and most populated city is Bamako.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Mali?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Mali on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Mali article.

questions.proof: Mali is bordered by Algeria on the North, Niger on the east, Burkina Faso and the Côte d'Ivoire on the south, Guinea on the south-west, and Senegal and Mauritania on the west.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Mali?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Demographics” part of the Mali article.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “As of a July _____ estimate, Mali had a population of approximately 21.9 million people.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Mali article.

questions.proof: As of a July 2021 estimate, Mali had a population of approximately 21.9 million people.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “_____ gave Mali the names French Sudan and the Sudanese Republic.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “gave”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Mali article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: France gave Mali the names French Sudan and the Sudanese Republic.
